messages:
dana: Quick share — ran a 6h perf sweep on the continuous batcher against the long/short synthetic mix. Seeing persistent token-starve for mid-tier tenants when sequences >1024 are present.

kevin: ugh. is this the KV-warmup case where long requests evict cached prefixes?

maria: yep. trace looked like: long seqs grab the fastpath kernels, but because they hold slots longer the batcher coalesces lots of short jobs behind them. short tenants wait multiple cycles.

dana: summary of the key signals I captured:
- burstiness: short traffic bursts get queued 3-7 batches behind long windows
- kernel affinity: fastpath kernels prefer long attention patterns, so they often lock slab for 120-300ms
- kv-hit-rate: tenants with warm prefixes keep 1.5x higher throughput; newcomers see kv miss churn

kevin: can you paste the flame/trace snippet?

maria: here — bolded the queue hold points:
```
[batcher] assemble_batch: tenant=T123 size=8 tokens=64-8192 window=200ms
[kern] select: long_fastpath -> slot A
[kv] evict: prefix=P45 tenant=T456
[batcher] commit_batch: latency=312ms
```

ryan: perf-bot flagged a regression after the kernel-selection refactor (r: infra/fastpath-switch). The 95p latency delta correlates with that change.

perf-bot: Regression detected: 95p latency +18% for mixed long/short workloads since deploy 2026-02-11. Suspected components: continuous-batcher v2, kernel-selector v1.3.

anya: thoughts: we shouldn't bias assignment purely on kernel suitability. need fairness knobs: token-budget floor per tenant, short-seq weight, or bounded hold time per slot.

kevin: proposal A (simple): impose max-hold-ms per slot of 120ms for any single batch. If a long batch would exceed, split it (maybe by forcing kernel fallback). Pros: limits head-of-line blocking. Cons: might lower long-path throughput.

maria: proposal B (budget): give each tenant a rolling token-credit with two buckets: short and long. Short jobs consume from short bucket first; long jobs can borrow but trigger backpressure if borrow > X. This keeps short bursts served.

dana: we tried a prototype of B in staging last week. Observed 40% reduction in short-tenant median latency and 6% throughput loss for long tenants. KV hit stability improved because we reduced eviction churn.

ryan: interesting — do we have telemetry to show kv eviction rate per tenant pre/post?

maria: yes. snapshot:
```
pre: kv_evictions/min = 12.4 global, top-10 tenants responsible 72%
post: kv_evictions/min = 4.7 global, top-10 tenants 54%
```

kevin: how about kernel-selection hybrid — prefer fastpath only if estimated hold < threshold. Otherwise force compatibility kernel that yields smaller per-request GPU residency. Could be metricized as "expected-hold-ms" computed from seq-length and kv-hit estimate.

anya: sounds good. need a conservative estimator first. maybe use 95p sequence length for tenant + current KV-hit ratio to predict.

dana: implementation checklist I propose:
1) add token-credit buckets (short/long) + refill policy (per-minute)
2) add max-hold-ms guard in batch allocator
3) kernel selector: expected-hold estimator + fallback policy
4) telemetry: per-tenant kv-evictions, batching-delay histogram, kernel-switch count

ryan: also add an experiment flag so we can A/B per region/instance class. We don't want a global flip until results stable.

maria: we should simulate with the workload replay harness first. I can run 48h mixed replay tomorrow and feed results.

kevin: metrics to watch in canary: short-tenant p50/p95, long-tenant throughput, overall tokens/s, kv_evictions/min, kernel-fallback-rate.

dana: note: edge case — tenant pinned models with large kv footprints may get unfairly penalized by token budget. We need an override to map high-SLA tenants to reserved credits (Dedicated customers).

anya: agreed. reserved credits + telemetry-based reclaiming for unused reserved slots.

perf-bot: Canary plan created: canary/continuous-batcher-fairness/2026-03-15. Targets: reduce short-tenant p95 by 30% without >10% throughput loss for long tenants.

ryan: next actions
- maria: run replay + produce A/B dashboard (due EOD 2026-03-16)
- dana: implement max-hold-ms guard and token-credit quickswitch (PR draft)
- kevin: add estimator proto in kernel selector
- anya: add reserved-credit exception logic for Dedicated tenants

kevin: one more note — update runbooks for fallback; when kernel-fallback-rate > 20% we should trigger an alert (possible under-provisioning).

maria: ack. will include that in dashboards.

dana: thanks all. will post a short postmortem-style summary after the canary ends. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy scheduled to canary cluster 3 at 2026-03-15T03:00Z (rolling). Release: continuous-batcher-fairness-v1.

kevin: appreciate the quick loop. if staging replay looks good, let's run a 72h canary before org-wide rollout.

anya: SGTM.

maria: uploading raw traces to s3://redwood-perf/batcher-fairness/1741112222/ — ping me for access.

dana: closing the thread for now, will reopen with results.
